title: Install a spark plug in a recessed cylinder-head well with a socket tool and seat its ignition coil
instruction: Take the spark plug socket tool, capture the spark plug from its staging tray, lower it into the cylinder head well and thread it home. Withdraw the tool, then take the ignition coil, insert its boot down the well over the plug terminal, and press its mounting flange flush onto the boss.
context: Automotive service technicians and mechanics (SOC 49-3023, 760,000+ US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2023) regularly replace spark plugs and ignition coils during scheduled tune-ups, misfire diagnoses, and engine servicing. In overhead-cam cylinder heads, spark plugs sit recessed in narrow wells. Mechanics use specialized spark-plug sockets with internal rubber retention inserts to capture the ceramic insulator, lower the plug into the well without dropping it (which cracks the brittle ceramic insulator or bends the ground electrode gap, causing cylinder misfires), thread home square, and pull the tool free. The coil-on-plug (COP) unit is then guided down the well to seat over the plug terminal and pressed flush to seal against water intrusion and align its mounting bolt hole. Dropping the plug, cocking the coil boot, or failing to seat either part scores 0.
setup: Dual YAM arm station (table z=0.7475 m). Fixed cylinder head trainer fixture (Toyota 1NZ-FE / Honda R18A style DOHC section, OEM 11101-21030, 180x140x40 mm) at (0.26, 0.0, z=0.7475 m) with authentic recessed spark plug well (30 mm bore, 30 mm deep, thread entry z=0.7635 m, M14x1.25 seat at z=0.7575 m) and adjacent M6 coil mounting boss at (0.295, 0.0, z=0.7875 m). Spark plug (NGK BKR6E / M14x1.25 thread, 16 mm hex collar, 42 mm tall, 35 g) upright in tray at (0.22, -0.12 m). Socket tool (16 mm hex cup with rubber insert, 25 mm extension, T-handle, 75 g) in cradle at (0.20, -0.20 m). Coil-on-plug unit (Denso 673-2301 style, silicone boot, mounting ear, 90 g) on stand at (0.22, 0.18 m).
scoring: 0 if spark plug drops onto table outside tray/well. Otherwise: 0.25 if spark plug captured and lifted clear; 0.50 if plug threaded home (M14x1.25 pitch-coupled descent down to seat) with tool clear; 0.75 if coil boot enters well mouth over threaded plug with tool clear; 1.0 if plug threaded home in seat, tool parked in cradle, coil boot seated over plug terminal with ear flush within 1.5 mm of boss, arms clear (>20 mm), and motionless hold. Post-run verification: plug thread torque-stop verified by depth gage; coil ear flush confirmed by overhead camera.
reset_notes: Extract ignition coil from well, extract spark plug with socket tool, return plug to tray, socket tool to cradle, and coil to stand.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies (240 Hz). Recessed hollow cylinder head well constructed via segmented perimeter walls with internal bottom shoulder. Spark plug threading simulates genuine M14x1.25 mm helical pitch (1.25 mm axial descent per 2*pi rad clockwise turn; 3.5 mm travel = ~2.8 turns). Compliant retention socket modeled with 4 N retention joint. Coil seating requires boot insertion over terminal and ear flush seating on boss <= 1.5 mm. Instantaneous live evaluation with defect latch on dropped plug.
no_video_reason: Untrained zero-shot Dream-1 policy fails to coordinate bimanual socket tool capture, recessed well entry, M14x1.25 thread rotation, and COP coil insertion within 800 steps (score: 0.00). Full-score bimanual execution demonstrated via scripted policy demo.mp4.
